name: Dappen Black Forest Tapp Tarock
description: Dappen is a complex trick-taking Tarock game for 6 or 7 players, traditional to the Upper Black Forest region of southwest Germany. It is played with Cego cards and features one player (the 'Dappener') playing alone against a team formed by all other participants, using a 12-card talon known as the 'Dapp'.

content.text: Dappen is a complex trick-taking Tarock game for 6 or 7 players, traditional to the Upper Black Forest region of southwest Germany. It is played with Cego cards and features one player (the 'Dappener') playing alone against a team formed by all other participants, using a 12-card talon known as the 'Dapp'.
Dappen originated in the early 19th century in the Upper Black Forest region of Germany. It remained a local oral tradition, undocumented by card game scholars outside the region until 2024.

Minimum Players: 6
Maximum Players: 7
Optimal Players: 6 or 7
Partnerships: One vs. Team

Type: Cego Tarot deck
Number of Cards: 54 (22 trumps/Tarocks, 32 suit cards)
Suits: French (Clubs, Spades, Hearts, Diamonds)
54 Cego cards, scoring chips or paper.
A 12-card talon (Dapp) is dealt first (usually in two batches of 6). The remaining cards are dealt to the players (7 cards each for 6 players, 6 cards each for 7 players).

items.text: Furtwangen (Klausmann): Full rules with Solo and Dappen bidding, compulsory dappen, Ulti, gstiesieren, and full or half game scoring.

Breitnau: No compulsory dappen; if all pass the hand is thrown in. No Ulti or gstiesieren. Stupfen (push) over strecken. Payment: difference from 40 multiplied by contract factor then rounded up to next 10.

Buchenbach: Six players only. Extra bids: Ein Hannes (one king), Zwei Hannes (two kings), Geiß (trump 1). First three tricks: Gstieß, then 21, then 1 must be played by holder; others must play 1-point trumps if able.
